name: Cacio e Pepe Mac in a Garlic Parm Bread Bowl
desc: Peppery cacio e pepe style mac and cheese served in a round loaf toasted with roasted garlic Parmesan butter.

source.title: Cacio e Pepe Mac in a Garlic Parm Bread Bowl
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 1 head garlic, for roasting (you need 3 roasted cloves)
1 large round crusty loaf (about 1 1/2 lb boule)
1 lb short pasta, such as elbows or cavatappi
1 tbsp kosher salt, for the pasta water
1/2 cup shredded sharp cheddar or Gruyère, grated from the block
1/2 tsp kosher salt, or to taste

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Slice the top off the garlic head, drizzle with the olive oil, wrap in foil, and roast 1 hr until soft and golden. Leave the oven on.
Squeeze out 3 roasted cloves (save the rest) and mash them into the softened butter with the Italian seasoning, red pepper flakes, salt, grated Parmesan and basil.

Cut a lid off the top of the loaf and hollow it out, leaving walls about 3/4 in thick. Spread the garlic butter over the inside and the cut side of the lid, sprinkle with the shaved Parmesan, and bake on a sheet pan 10-15 min until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to a boil with the kosher salt. Cook the pasta until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water and drain.
Toast the peppercorns in a dry skillet over medium heat 3-4 min until fragrant, then crush them coarsely in a mortar or under a heavy pan.

In a large saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook 30 sec. Add the crushed pepper and cook 1 min. Slowly whisk in the milk and cook 3-4 min, whisking, until it steams and thickens slightly.
Turn off the heat. Stir in the Parmesan and cheddar until melted, season with salt, then stir in the pasta. Loosen with a splash of pasta water if needed.
Spoon the mac into the bread bowl and serve right away, with the extra in a dish alongside.
tips: Toast the pepper in the roux to bloom it.
A Cozy Kitchen's cacio e pepe mac uses 6 tbsp each of butter and flour for the same 3 cups of milk; with 1 tbsp each this sauce stays loose, so use more roux if you want it thicker.
